title: Heat and Temperature
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Heat and Temperature Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Distinguish between heat and temperature using the particle theory; describe conduction, convection and radiation; explain how conductors and insulators are used to control heat transfer. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Heat in the Environment)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets on heat and temperature, the particle theory, conduction, convection, radiation, insulators and thermal expansion. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat flows from warmer to cooler.
key_sub: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation; insulators slow it down.
body_html:
How to think about it

Temperature measures how fast particles are moving. Heat is energy moving from a warmer object to a cooler one.

  • Conduction: through a solid, by particles bumping. Convection: by moving liquids and gases. Radiation: as waves, even through space.
  • Metals are good conductors; air, wool, foam and plastic are insulators.
  • Most substances expand when heated and contract when cooled.
Example

How does the Sun's heat reach Earth?

space is almost empty

Answer: radiation

Example

Why does a metal spoon in hot tea get hot?

particles bump through the metal

Answer: conduction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking 'cold' flows into things.
  • Thinking heat and temperature are the same.
  • Thinking insulators make things warm (they only slow heat flow).

faq.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
faq.a: Temperature tells how hot something is. Heat is the energy that moves from hotter to colder things.

faq.q: What are the three ways heat moves?
faq.a: Conduction (through solids), convection (by moving fluids) and radiation (as waves).

faq.q: Why do sweaters keep us warm?
faq.a: They trap air, which is an insulator, so our body heat escapes more slowly.

items.e: The hotter object loses heat to the colder one.

items.q: Priya compares two things. Which has a higher temperature: a bathtub of warm water (40 °C) or a cup of hot tea (80 °C)?

items.q: Ava compares two things. Which has more thermal energy: a big pot of soup (60 °C) or a spoonful of the same soup (60 °C)?

a spoonful of the same soup (60 °C)
items.e: Same temperature, but the big pot has many more particles, so it has more total thermal energy.

items.q: Why are pot handles made of plastic or wood?
